thesis: Fervo's Aug 12 Q2 print and guidance cut (2027 revenue to $60-80M) cited transmission curtailment at Cape Station, driving shares to a fresh 52-week low on 9.6x average volume; this suggests the market is repricing near-term monetization timing rather than the underlying resource, even though the Sept 1 396MW Google PPA reaffirms long-term offtake demand regardless of the curtailment bottleneck. thesis: Intel's decline mixes a confirmed GAAP Q2 net loss of $11B (mostly a one-time CHIPS Act mark-to-market charge) and continuing Foundry operating losses with a just-closed $20B stock offering priced at $95 (Aug 10-12) that has diluted shareholders and left shares trading below the offer price; this suggests the pullback is a real reversion from an extreme H1 run-up compounded by ongoing dilution and foundry cash burn, even though Q2 revenue grew 25% and Q3 guidance beat expectations. thesis: AMD's decline traces mainly to sector/competitive sentiment shocks — an unconfirmed Reuters report on China's DeepSeek developing its own AI chip, Elon Musk's comment that SpaceX would buy AI chips exclusively from Nvidia, and a late-August Fed-driven semiconductor selloff — rather than any AMD-specific adverse disclosure; this suggests the pullback is sentiment/macro-driven, since AMD's own confirmed Q2 2026 results (Aug 4) beat estimates on both EPS and revenue with management guiding to accelerating 2H26 data-center growth and Microsoft added to the Helios customer roster. invalidation: Q3 2026 data-center guidance is walked back, or the DeepSeek/competitive-chip reports are confirmed by AMD's own disclosures as a material demand threat

thesis: Dell's rise and volume spike track confirmed AI-server momentum — record Q1 FY27 AI-server revenue (+757% YoY) and an Aug 4 disclosed $10B AI-factory partnership (Volta) — with today's Q2 FY27 print also confirming the trend (record $47.0B revenue, record EPS); this suggests durable, disclosed demand, even though the Aug 31 volume spike itself coincides mainly with pre-earnings options positioning and margin-compression concerns (gross margin fell to 17.8% from 21.1% YoY) rather than a fresh confirmed catalyst on that specific day. invalidation: Material weakness remediation stalls or the SEC subpoena escalates to a formal action, or AI-server gross margin compression continues without an offsetting revenue mix shift

thesis: SPCX's decline traces mainly to its confirmed Aug 4 Q2 print, where a 92% YoY revenue beat and narrowing losses were overshadowed by a ~6x YoY capex jump to $18.37B, compounded by an analyst Sell initiation (DZ Bank, mid-August) and a broader August growth-stock selloff, plus a scheduled, prospectus-disclosed insider lock-up unlock running through December; this suggests the pressure is a valuation/capital-efficiency and technical-supply story rather than any confirmed fraud, litigation, insolvency, or governance failure. Even though the underlying business shows genuine growth (adj. EBITDA +191% YoY), the combination of an unproven AI-capex payoff thesis, independent fair-value estimates below the current price, and continuing scheduled share-supply releases into year-end argues for staying out.
invalidation: Capex efficiency/ROI on AI infrastructure becomes demonstrable in a subsequent quarterly print, or the lock-up unlock schedule completes without sustained selling pressure
